Fed & Policy Watch
  • FOMC minutes for the Oct 27-28 meeting are scheduled for Wed Nov 18 at 2:00 PM ET. Minutes are not a policy decision. The next material U.S. releases beyond the one-week calendar are GDP (Second Estimate) and October Personal Income and Outlays at 8:30 AM ET on Nov 25, listed by both the New York Fed and BEA.
  • The New York Fed December calendar schedules Employment Situation on Dec 4, CPI on Dec 10 and PPI on Dec 15, all at 8:30 AM ET. The Federal Reserve Board calendar lists the next FOMC decision on Dec 9 at 2:00 PM and press conference at 2:30 PM ET. CPI and PPI are distinct releases.
  • Liquidity/rates context: SOFR 3.89% effective Nov 10, NFCI -0.455 for week ending Nov 6, MOVE 98.43 on Nov 12, and official 10-year Treasury close 5.10% on Nov 12. SOFR and NFCI are lagged observations, not live funding measures.
Omissions and Watch
  • Date/event conflict check: New York Fed November calendar verifies today's PPI, not CPI; its Nov 17-18 retail, inventories, construction and pending-home-sales dates agree with Census/NAR schedules. BEA and New York Fed agree on Nov 25 at 8:30 AM for Q3 GDP second estimate and October personal income/outlays. Board calendar identifies the Nov 18 FOMC minutes release. No date/time conflict was found among the selected rows.
  • New York Fed calendar lists Business Leaders Survey on Nov 17 and Outlook-at-Risk on Nov 18 without a release time; neither is assigned an invented time or included in timed rows. Other events are selected, not exhaustive. Treasury auction rows are limited to the specific dated securities verified in the TreasuryDirect response, not a complete auction slate.
  • BLS dates/times use the New York Fed Economic Indicators Calendar; bls.gov was not requested. Periods are included only where checked primary sources state them; otherwise they are marked period not stated. EIA schedule confirms the Nov 13 natural-gas holiday exception and the standard Wed petroleum release time. No CME contract-hours or settlement details were verified.
  • Classifier provisional unmatched rows (SCE Credit Access Survey, Imports and Exports, Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization, Initial Claims, and Michigan Consumer Survey Final) remain Medium and are visibly flagged; no overrides. Self-test passed. No verified unscheduled policy/geopolitical watch item from this run; that is not a full headline-risk review.
  • Primary sources checked: New York Fed November/December calendars, SOFR API and Empire State Survey; Federal Reserve Board November/December calendars and H.4.1; BEA; Census; NAR; EIA petroleum and natural-gas schedules; TreasuryDirect; Chicago Fed NFCI; U.S. Treasury yield data; Philadelphia Fed and University of Michigan releases. Snapshot uses single-source Yahoo Finance charts, with observation times and prior bars stated above.
Trading Strategy Note | ES Futures
BASE CASE
ES is fractionally above Thursday's completed daily bar overnight, while SPY's Thursday close slipped 0.35%. VIX rose to 18.70, MOVE remains moderate at 98.43, and the 10-year yield advanced to 5.10%. PPI, energy data and selected Fed releases are ahead today, with retail sales and FOMC minutes next week; expect event-sensitive two-way risk. Monitor rates, breadth and depth rather than treating the thin overnight move as direction. Scenario framing only, not a trade signal.
INVALIDATION
Reassess if PPI, energy data or Fed communication materially reprices yields, volatility expands against the current overnight move, or ES price action lacks confirmation from breadth, rates or depth. No unsupported levels or targets supplied. Refresh quotes and verify intended contract specifications before execution.
